clue.text: Uplifting song from worker by border

indicators.note: by means next to, so the second piece sits right beside the first

parts.note: the worker ant is crosswordland's standard worker
a hem is the finished border of cloth

explanation.surface: A rousing song composed by a labourer living near a frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: An anthem is a stirring song of praise or loyalty, sung to raise spirits.

clue.text: Shelter, then sun is out

indicators.note: out suggests things put out of place, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of all three words

explanation.surface: Take cover, because the sun has come out.
explanation.definitionFit: A Nissen hut is a corrugated-iron semicircular hut used as a wartime shelter or barracks.

clue.text: Hang Henry More?!

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
over means more than, as in over a hundred

explanation.surface: An exclamation about exhibiting work by the sculptor Henry Moore.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry Moore was a British sculptor, but here the name splits into Henry and More.
explanation.definitionFit: To hover is to hang suspended in the air, as a hawk does.

clue.text: Cruelly spurned, mama and nan in play

indicators.note: cruelly suggests rough treatment, so the letters are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: Mother and grandmother are harshly rejected in a theatre production.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'and' between mama and nan is a joining word, not part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Man and Superman is a 1903 comedy by George Bernard Shaw.

clue.text: Powerless, girl, British, against the Parisian

indicators.note: against means leaning up beside, so the final piece is placed alongside the others

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for British

explanation.surface: A list of a weak girl's attributes: British, and opposed to the man from Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unable lacks the capacity or power to act.

clue.text: She may attend to babe in arms due for a change

indicators.note: for a change asks for something different, so the letters move about

parts.note: the letters of all three words

explanation.surface: A carer holds an infant who needs a nappy change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'babe in arms' reads as one phrase, but the definition stops at babe.
explanation.definitionFit: A nursemaid is a woman employed to look after young children.

clue.text: Take a swim in city close to seaside

indicators.note: close is read as the end, so we keep only the last letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Going for a dip in a town near the coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close to' looks like nearby but means the end of seaside.
explanation.definitionFit: To bathe, in British usage, is to swim in the sea or a river.

clue.text: Wild sheep ahead of us in ancient Greek city

indicators.note: wild means untamed and disordered, so the letters are rearranged
ahead of means placed in front of the next piece

explanation.surface: Untamed sheep running ahead of us through an old Greek city.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephesus was an ancient Greek city on the coast of Asia Minor, now in Turkey.

clue.text: A cocktail's qualities, nurse recollected

indicators.note: recollected is read as collected again, the letters gathered up in new order

explanation.surface: A nurse remembered how good a particular cocktail was.
explanation.definitionFit: A tequila sunrise is a cocktail of tequila, orange juice and grenadine.

clue.text: It may lead to a divorce if they've arsenic prepared!

definitions.text: It may lead to a divorce

indicators.note: prepared suggests something mixed up or cooked, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of both words, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A spouse with poison ready to hand suggests a marriage heading for the rocks.
explanation.walkthrough: The poison joke fits the definition: a murderous spouse is a darker route out of marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: The seven-year itch is the supposed restlessness that tempts a married person to stray, a common cause of divorce.

clue.text: Damage small vehicle

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A little car has been dented.
explanation.definitionFit: To scar is to mark or disfigure, a form of lasting damage.

clue.text: Ordinary boy following Guevara and Villa, initially

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the boy goes at the end
initially points to the opening letter of the word just before it

explanation.surface: An everyday lad trailing two revolutionaries, Che Guevara and Pancho Villa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordinary' looks like an adjective for the boy, but in heraldry an ordinary is a simple standard shape on a shield.
explanation.definitionFit: A chevron, the inverted V band on a shield, is one of the heraldic ordinaries.

clue.text: Ineffectual advice from a conservationist?

definitions.meaning: second meaning, split in two: a plea to consume less

explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as two words, USE LESS, and it is what a conservationist urges.
explanation.definitionFit: Something useless achieves nothing, which is what ineffectual means.

clue.text: Tries within existing practice

indicators.note: within says one word sits inside another

parts.note: a judge tries, or hears, a case

explanation.surface: Attempts made during an ongoing training session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tries' looks like attempts, as in rugby, but it is the legal verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehearsal is a practice run of a performance before the real thing.

clue.text: Trees, all the rage in Hants town

explanation.surface: Trees are suddenly fashionable in a Hampshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: Hants is the standard abbreviation for Hampshire, the English county.
explanation.definitionFit: Aldershot is a garrison town in Hampshire, home of the British Army.

clue.text: States opposed? Not quite

indicators.note: not quite means falling just short, so the word loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A question about whether some nations are in opposition, answered with a hedge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'States' looks like countries; it is the verb, to declare.
explanation.definitionFit: To aver is to assert firmly, so avers is a synonym of states.

clue.text: Dress up bride more elaborately

indicators.note: elaborately suggests something worked over, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Instructions to make the bride's outfit fancier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dress up' reads as clothing the bride, but it means to embellish a story.
explanation.definitionFit: To embroider a tale is to embellish it with invented details, to dress it up.

clue.text: Old hat found in cupboard at Eddie's

indicators.note: found in says the letters are lying inside the words that follow

parts.note: spans the end of cupboard, the whole of at and the start of Eddie's

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned hat turned up in a cupboard at Eddie's house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old hat' reads as a battered piece of headgear, but it is an idiom for outmoded.
explanation.definitionFit: Old hat is an idiom for stale or outmoded, which is what dated means.

clue.text: Mitty type, gloomy ringing me

indicators.note: ringing means forming a ring around, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: drear is a poetic form of dreary

explanation.surface: A daydreaming sort phones me in a downbeat mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ringing' suggests a phone call; it means surrounding.
explanation.definitionFit: Walter Mitty is the fantasising hero of a Thurber story, a byword for a daydreamer.

clue.text: Pals booed performing a quick dance

indicators.note: performing suggests putting on an act, so the letters are made to take new positions

explanation.surface: Friends jeered while someone did a fast dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The paso doble is a brisk Latin ballroom dance modelled on a bullfight march.

clue.text: Bridge player, female, leaving banquet

indicators.note: leaving means departing, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A woman at the card table walks out of a dinner party.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge the four players are named by compass point, so East is one of them.

clue.text: Envoy in capital brought over sovereign

indicators.note: brought over means turned over, so the whole combination is read backwards
in tells us one word goes inside another

parts.note: a rep, short for representative, acts as an envoy

explanation.surface: A diplomat in the capital arranged for a monarch to come over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought over' looks like transporting the sovereign, but it turns the whole envoy-in-capital assembly back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: An emperor is a supreme ruler, so a sovereign in the highest sense.

clue.text: Pier collapsing — 50 in danger

indicators.note: collapsing means falling apart, so the letters fall into a new order

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for 50

explanation.surface: A seaside pier is falling down with fifty people at risk.
explanation.definitionFit: Peril means serious and immediate danger.

clue.text: Highly strung member of the Crazy Gang, American

parts.note: Jimmy Nervo was one of the Crazy Gang

explanation.surface: An American who belonged to a madcap comedy troupe and was very tense.
explanation.walkthrough: The Crazy Gang was a British comedy troupe of the 1930s to 1960s; Nervo and Knox were one of its double acts.
explanation.definitionFit: A highly strung person is excitable and easily upset, which is what nervous describes.

clue.text: Poke around bottom of Tigris for perch

indicators.note: around means going about the outside of another piece

parts.note: to root about is to poke around searching

indicators.note: the bottom of a down word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Rummaging on the riverbed of the Tigris for a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perch' tempts as the fish, which suits the river, but it is a bird's resting place.
explanation.definitionFit: A roost is a place where birds settle to rest, a perch.

clue.text: Unfortunately harms girl in plant

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things going wrong, so the letters fall out of order

explanation.surface: Sadly, someone damages a girl who is inside a factory or a greenhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: The girl's name is itself a flower, which helps tie the second half to the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The marsh marigold is a yellow-flowered wetland plant, also called the kingcup.

clue.text: Describe an event, clergyman being beheaded

indicators.note: beheaded means losing the head, so the first letter is cut off

parts.note: a prelate is a senior clergyman such as a bishop

explanation.surface: An account of the time a churchman was executed.
explanation.definitionFit: To relate something is to narrate or tell it, as you would an event.

clue.text: Complete set of religious books discovered in Ireland

indicators.note: discovered in means found sitting inside the next word

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for Ireland

explanation.surface: A full collection of sacred texts turned up in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Entire means whole, with nothing missing, so it is a synonym of complete.
